chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Hisham narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Sa'd ibn Zarif from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, intends to punish all the people of the earth if they commit sins and perform evil deeds. But when He sees the elderly, whose steps are frail, going to prayer, and the children learning the Quran, He has mercy on them and delays that punishment from them.
ai.seo_question: What causes Allah to delay punishing humanity for their sins?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates the mechanism of divine patience (*al-hilm*), where the collective punishment of humanity is suspended by the intercession of two specific groups: the elderly who persist in prayer despite physical decline, and the youth engaged in Quranic learning. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of worship across generations as a tangible cause for averting divine wrath and securing mercy for the broader community.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3.  Amirul Momineen (a.s.) says, “Whenever people of the earth  commit  sins  or  get  involved  in  wrong  deeds,  the Almighty Allah intends to send down His chastisement on the  people  of the world.  However  when  He  sees  elderly people praying and young children learning Quran, He feels pity on them and does not send down His chastisement.”
